newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Jackson marries in Sydney, bride wears white.
newsitem.headline: Jackson marries in Sydney, bride wears white.

text.p: American pop superstar Michael Jackson married his pregnant girlfriend on Friday before a handful of friends in a luxury Sydney hotel suite, his tour publicist said.

"The bride wore white. I don't know if it was a wedding dress. I don't know how Michael was dressed," Brian Walsh told Reuters. "The Jackson group has now confirmed the marriage and said it would not be making any further comment."

Jackson, 38, married former nurse Debbie Rowe in a civil ceremony in his presidential suite at the Sheraton-on-the-Park Hotel, said Walsh. He did not know whether the couple exchanged any special wedding vows.
Jackson's marriage to the 37-year-old nurse came a few hours after he finished his first sell-out concert of the Australian leg of his HIStory world tour.
"They were married in a small ceremony early this morning at Michael's hotel," Walsh said.

"The ceremony was attended by a few friends and people from the tour entourage. Debbie has known Michael for a long time and has been with the entourage for a while and they have a lot of friends in common," he said.
In a written statement distributed on the Internet global computer network, Jackson said: "Please respect our privacy and let us enjoy this wonderful and exciting time".
The wedding took place only 10 days after Jackson announced Rowe, who nursed him while he was being treated for a rare skin disorder, was to give birth to his child early next year.
Jackson denied news reports that Rowe had been artificially inseminated and that he paid US$500,000 to carry his child.
This is second time that Jackson -- known for a bizarre fantasy lifestyle surrounded by children and with a pet chimpanzee -- has been married in secret.

In January, Lisa Marie Presley, daughter of late rock and roll legend Elvis, filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences 20 months after they were married in secret in the Dominican Republic.

Shortly before that marriage, Jackson was embroiled in a legal battle after allegations that he sexually molested a young boy. Jackson vehemently denied the claims and prosecutors said in late 1994 that they were not pressing criminal charges.
Jackson agreed earlier that year to pay the boy a multi-million dollar settlement in return for droppng a civil lawsuit against him.

Rowe has reportedly been divorced for eight years from her first husband and lives in an apartment in the Los Angeles suburb of Van Nuys. She is said to have met Jackson 15 years ago while working for a doctor who was treating the entertainer for the skin condition vitiligo.

Walsh said Jackson and his new bride -- who is six months pregnant -- will spend their honeymoon in Australia, but he did not say whether the honeymoon would last for longer than Jackson's current concert tour. Jackson has concert engagements in Australia for the rest of November.
"Michael and his bride will spend their honeymoon period in Australia," he said. "As has been the case in this tour, Michael wants to get out and meet as many fans as possible."

"The next public appearance for Michael will be when he appears at the premiere of his movie Ghost at 9.00 p.m. (1000GMT)," said Walsh, adding he did not know whether Rowe would accompany Jackson to the film premiere.
"We are just being notified of the itinerary day by day."
Jackson has another concert scheduled for Sydney on Saturday night and will appear on the steps of the Sydney Opera House on Sunday to receive an award from his record company Sony.
A giant fibreglass bust of Jackson will be floated past the Opera House during the ceremony.
